cards.title: Respectful interaction: Classmates with physical disabilities
facts: A wheelchair, crutch, or white cane is an extension of a person's personal body space; touching or pushing it without permission is a violation.
Treat classmates with disabilities as complete equals: speak directly to them at eye level, not to their caregiver or companion.
do: Always ask 'Would you like some assistance?' and wait for their answer before grabbing or pushing a wheelchair
Sit down on a chair when having a long conversation so you are at comfortable eye level with a wheelchair user
Keep hallways, ramps, and classroom doorways completely clear of backpacks and desks
dont: NEVER lean on, grab, or push someone's wheelchair without their explicit consent
NEVER talk down to someone with a physical disability as if they are a helpless toddler

myths.statement: If you see a classmate in a wheelchair, you should immediately grab the handles and push them without asking to be helpful.
myths.truth: A wheelchair is personal bodily space. Grabbing it without asking is alarming and disrespectful. Always ask permission first.

quiz.q: What is the polite and respectful protocol before assisting a classmate who uses mobility aids?
options: Grab their crutches and carry them
Ask politely if they would like assistance, and respect their answer if they say 'No thanks, I've got this'
Ignore them completely
Push their wheelchair as fast as possible
quiz.explanation: Dignity means respecting autonomy: always ask first, listen to their specific preference, and honor their independence.

situations: At the school entrance ramp at {at}, {name} sees a classmate in a wheelchair preparing to navigate an incline.
scenario.question: How should {name} offer support respectfully?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Walk up, make friendly eye contact, and ask: 'Hi, would you like a hand with the ramp today?'
rubric.note: Offers assistance politely while respecting bodily autonomy.
rubric.keys: ask permission first|friendly eye contact|respect autonomy

rubric.point: Wait for their response and follow their specific directions on how to hold or push the chair
rubric.keys: wait for response|follow directions

rubric.point: Ensure the ramp pathway is clear of discarded water bottles or student bags
rubric.keys: clear pathway|remove obstacles

dangerous: grab wheelchair handles from behind without speaking
pat classmate on head like a child
stare awkwardly and walk away

sources.name: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD)

cards.title: Communicating with Deaf peers: Eye contact, light, and sign basics
facts: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people communicate through rich visual languages; Indian Sign Language (ISL) is a complete, expressive linguistic system.
When speaking with someone who lip-reads or signs, facial expressions, clear lighting, and facing them directly are essential.
do: Tap gently on their shoulder or wave your hand in their field of vision to get their attention politely
Face the person directly in good lighting so your mouth and facial expressions are clearly visible
Learn basic Indian Sign Language (ISL) signs for 'Hello', 'Thank you', 'Friend', and 'Help'
dont: Never cover your mouth with your hand or turn your back while speaking to someone who lip-reads
Never shout loudly into the ear of a deaf person; shouting distorts lip shapes and does not help

myths.statement: Shouting at the top of your lungs into a deaf person's ear helps them understand what you are saying.
myths.truth: Shouting distorts facial and lip movements and can cause painful acoustic feedback in hearing aids. Speak at normal volume facing them.

quiz.q: What is the polite way to get the attention of a deaf or hard-of-hearing classmate in a noisy room?
options: Throwing a pencil at their head
A gentle tap on the shoulder or a friendly wave within their visual field
Screaming their name repeatedly
Turning off the room lights violently
quiz.explanation: Gentle visual or tactile cues respect dignity and establish natural communication without aggression.

situations: During group project discussion in the classroom at {at}, a hard-of-hearing classmate is looking down while another student speaks quickly from across the table.
scenario.question: How should {name} facilitate inclusive communication?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Gently wave a hand in their view to signal the discussion is starting and face them directly
rubric.note: Ensures visual engagement and mutual presence.
rubric.keys: gentle wave|face them directly|good lighting

rubric.point: Speak at a natural, steady pace with clear lip movement without exaggerated shouting
rubric.keys: steady pace|clear lip movement|do not shout

rubric.point: Write down key project decisions and bullet points in a shared notebook so nothing is missed
rubric.keys: write down key points|shared notebook

dangerous: exclude deaf peer from project
shout directly into their ear
talk behind their back

sources.name: Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre (ISLRTC)

cards.title: Accents and mother tongues: Linguistic diversity is India's strength
facts: An accent simply means a person has the brilliance and courage to speak more than one language.
India is home to over 19,500 spoken mother tongues and dialects; mocking someone's regional pronunciation is ignorant and deeply hurtful.
do: Appreciate that someone with an accent speaks their mother tongue PLUS another language
Focus on the content and meaning of what a peer is saying, never mock their phonetics or rhythm
If you do not understand a word, ask politely: 'Could you please repeat that last sentence?'
dont: Never imitate, mock, or exaggerate someone's regional accent for cheap laughs in class
Never judge someone's intelligence or capability by their fluency in English

myths.statement: People who speak English with a heavy regional mother-tongue accent are less intelligent and uneducated.
myths.truth: Accent has zero correlation with intelligence. Many world-renowned scientists and thinkers speak English as their third or fourth language.

quiz.q: What does having an accent when speaking English or Hindi genuinely signify?
options: That the person has poor memory
That the person is multilingual and mastered another rich mother tongue first
That they need medical treatment
That they cannot learn
quiz.explanation: Accents are the melodic footprint of a person's multilingual heritage and cognitive breadth.

situations: A new student from a different state speaks English with a regional inflection at {at}, and two classmates giggle and mock the pronunciation.
scenario.question: How should {name} respond?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Step in and say: 'His point was really interesting, let's listen to what he is actually saying'
rubric.note: Redirects attention to substantive ideas and halts mockery.
rubric.keys: listen to his point|halt mockery|stand up for peer

rubric.point: Engage the new student in conversation warmly, asking about their background and experiences
rubric.keys: engage warmly|ask about background|inclusive friendship

rubric.point: Remind peers privately that India's diverse mother tongues are a shared cultural treasure
rubric.keys: remind peers of linguistic diversity|cultural respect

dangerous: join in mocking the accent
laugh along to avoid being targeted
tell new student to stop talking

sources.name: National Education Policy (NEP) - Multilingualism and Cultural Harmony

cards.title: The buddy system: Making sure no newcomer sits alone
facts: Entering a new school where everyone already has established friend groups is one of the most intimidating experiences in childhood.
A single welcoming gesture—inviting a new peer to sit at your lunch table—can permanently change their school trajectory.
do: Take initiative: Walk over, introduce yourself, and say 'Hi, welcome to our class, I'm {name}'
Invite them to sit with you during lunch and guide them to science labs and water coolers
Introduce the new student to your other friends so their social circle broadens naturally
dont: Never stare at new students without saying hello or leave them wandering lost in corridors
Never treat new classmates as rivals or invaders in your established social circles

myths.statement: New students prefer being left completely alone in the corner for their first two months to adjust quietly.
myths.truth: Newcomers feel deep anxiety and isolation. A warm, friendly welcome immediately dispels fear and builds belonging.

quiz.q: What is the simplest and most powerful way to make a new classmate feel welcome on day one?
options: Stare at their shoes silently
Invite them to sit at your lunch table and show them where the library and labs are
Ask them why they left their old school
Ignore them completely
quiz.explanation: Sharing lunch and guiding them through physical school logistics creates immediate safety and comfort.

situations: On Monday morning at {at}, a new student stands alone against the corridor wall clutching their books, looking anxious as crowds rush past.
scenario.question: How should {name} act as an inclusive peer?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Walk up warmly, introduce yourself, and offer to show them to the homeroom classroom
rubric.keys: walk up warmly|introduce self|show homeroom

rubric.point: Invite them to sit together during recess and introduce them to two other friendly classmates
rubric.keys: invite to recess lunch|introduce to friends

rubric.point: Answer their questions about teachers, timetables, and locker locations with patience
rubric.keys: answer timetable questions|practical orientation

dangerous: walk past without looking
whisper with friends about their appearance
prank the new student

cards.title: Beyond stereotypes: Human potential has no gender
facts: Gender stereotypes restrict human potential: boys are pressured to suppress tears, while girls are discouraged from sports, coding, or leadership.
True equality recognizes that strength, sensitivity, scientific curiosity, empathy, and courage belong equally to all human beings.
do: Encourage girls in robotics, mathematics, cricket, and public debate leadership
Support boys in expressing emotions, cooking, artistic dance, and caregiving without mocking them
Divide classroom duties (cleaning, carrying chairs, technology setup) equally without gender segregation
dont: Never say 'You throw like a girl' or 'Boys don't cry'—both phrases enforce harmful myths
Never assume certain school subjects or careers belong exclusively to one gender

myths.statement: Boys are biologically wired to be good at math and coding, while girls are biologically wired only for languages and art.
myths.truth: Cognitive research shows zero innate difference in mathematical or scientific capability between boys and girls. Differences stem from social conditioning.

quiz.q: Why is telling a crying boy that 'Boys don't cry' psychologically harmful?
options: Because boys have more tears than girls
Because it teaches boys to bottle up normal human emotions, leading to emotional numbness and aggression
Because it makes them laugh
Because boys have no tear ducts
quiz.explanation: Suppressing emotions harms mental health. Emotional expression is a human trait, not a gender weakness.

situations: In the science lab at {at}, a male student laughs when a female classmate volunteers to be team captain for the robotics rover build.
scenario.question: How should {name} promote gender inclusion?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Affirm the female classmate's leadership role and support her captaincy based on competence
rubric.keys: support her captaincy|merit over bias|stand against stereotype

rubric.point: Point out that engineering and leadership belong to whoever has the passion and skill, regardless of gender
rubric.keys: engineering for everyone|passion and skill

rubric.point: Collaborate enthusiastically as a team player under her project direction
rubric.keys: collaborate under her direction|respectful teamwork

dangerous: tell female student to do paperwork instead
agree that girls cant build robots
boycott the project

sources.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development - Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

cards.title: Crushing body shaming: Defending peers against appearance bullying
facts: Body shaming targets weight, height, skin complexion, hair texture, or facial features, causing severe lifelong depression and eating disorders.
Cruel comments disguised as 'just a joke' are bullying; staying silent makes bystanders complicit in the harm.
do: Call out body shaming in the moment: 'That's not funny, let's not make comments about people's bodies'
Check in privately with the targeted person: 'Hey, what they said was awful, I don't agree with it at all'
Compliment peers on their character, wit, kindness, and effort rather than their physical measurements
dont: Never join in laughter when someone is mocked for their weight, skin color, or height
Never give unsolicited advice on dieting, skin lightening, or gym routines to peers

myths.statement: Making fun of a classmate's weight or dark skin is harmless banter as long as everyone laughs.
myths.truth: Body shaming inflicts deep emotional trauma and triggers self-loathing and eating disorders. Cruelty is never banter.

quiz.q: What is the most effective way for a bystander to stop appearance-based teasing in a group conversation?
options: Laugh along so you don't get teased next
Look at the person teasing and say calmly: 'We don't do body comments here, let's talk about something else'
Film the teasing and post it on social media
Start teasing the teaser's physical body
quiz.explanation: Clear, calm social boundaries set by peers extinguish bullying far faster than passive silence.

situations: In the school courtyard at {at}, a group of students loudly teases a classmate about their weight and height, calling them cruel nicknames.
scenario.question: How should {name} act as an upstander?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Speak up clearly to the group: 'Leave them alone, commenting on people's bodies is completely uncool'
rubric.note: Interrupts bullying behavior directly with moral courage.
rubric.keys: speak up clearly|leave them alone|body shaming uncool

rubric.point: Stand beside the targeted classmate and guide them away from the teasing circle
rubric.note: Provides physical solidarity and safe exit.
rubric.keys: stand beside classmate|guide away from circle

rubric.point: Spend the rest of lunch hanging out with them and reporting the bullying to a teacher if it repeats
rubric.note: Follows up with genuine friendship and institutional safety.
rubric.keys: hang out as friends|report persistent bullying

dangerous: join the laughter to fit in
film the bullying on your phone
tell the victim they should diet

sources.name: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) - Anti-Bullying Guidelines

cards.title: Every job has dignity: Respecting sanitation and domestic workers
facts: A society is judged by how it treats the people who keep it clean, fed, and running: domestic helpers, sweepers, drivers, and security guards.
Dignity of labor is a foundational democratic value; ordering workers around with disrespect reflects poorly on your character, not theirs.
do: Always address service workers, security guards, and domestic staff with polite honorifics (Bhaiya, Didi, Uncle, Aunty)
Say 'Thank you' and 'Please' when staff hand you clean water, sweep your classroom, or open gates
Clean up your own spills, return your own cafeteria trays, and never leave humiliating messes for staff
dont: Never talk down to domestic helpers or speak to them in commanding, rude tones
Never litter on school grounds with the arrogant thought: 'The sweeper is paid to clean this'

myths.statement: Because domestic workers and sweepers are paid wages, you do not need to show them basic politeness or say thank you.
myths.truth: Wages pay for labor, not for subservience. Dignity, kindness, and courtesy are fundamental human rights due to every worker.

quiz.q: What does leaving your trash scattered on a classroom floor because 'sweepers will clean it' demonstrate?
options: High personal wealth
A total lack of civic responsibility and disrespect for human labor
Superior education
Good efficiency
quiz.explanation: Respecting dignity of labor means minimizing other people's toil through personal accountability.

situations: In the school cafeteria at {at}, {name} sees a student deliberately spill curry on the floor, laugh, and shout at the cleaning staff: 'Come clean this quickly!'
scenario.question: How should {name} respond with civic dignity?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Pick up napkins and help wipe up the spill, apologizing to the cleaning staff member for the classmate's rudeness
rubric.note: Demonstrates humility and dignity of labor through action.
rubric.keys: help wipe up spill|apologize to staff|dignity of labor

rubric.point: Address the rude student firmly: 'Staff members are not your personal servants, treat people with respect'
rubric.note: Asserts civic and human boundaries against arrogance.
rubric.keys: staff not servants|treat with respect|confront arrogance

rubric.point: Thank the cleaning staff member warmly for keeping the cafeteria clean and healthy for all students
rubric.keys: thank cleaning staff warmly|affirm dignity

dangerous: laugh along with the rude student
kick curry further across floor
order staff to hurry up

sources.name: Ministry of Labour and Employment - Dignity of Labour Principles

cards.title: Bridging language gaps: Patience with peers learning a new tongue
facts: Students moving across states often struggle to express complex thoughts in Hindi or English while their intellect remains razor-sharp.
Mocking broken grammar or laughing at hesitations silences intelligent peers and creates deep academic trauma.
do: Give peers full, patient time to finish their sentences without interrupting or finishing their words
Use simple vocabulary, gestures, or visual diagrams when explaining concepts across language differences
Encourage and praise their courage in communicating in a second or third language
dont: Never laugh at grammatical mistakes or unusual word choices made by non-native speakers
Never roll your eyes or sigh loudly while someone is searching for a word in class

myths.statement: If a student struggles to speak English fluently in science class, it means they are incapable of understanding science.
myths.truth: Language is merely a tool for communication, not a measure of intelligence. Deep scientific concepts exist independently of English fluency.

quiz.q: How should you act when a classmate from another state hesitates while searching for words in English or Hindi?
options: Finish their sentence aggressively for them
Listen patiently with encouraging body language and give them time to express their thought
Tell them to sit down
Laugh at their grammar
quiz.explanation: Patience and warm non-verbal encouragement create psychological safety for language learners.

situations: During an environmental science seminar at {at}, a student who recently relocated from a rural district struggles to find English words to explain solar irrigation.
scenario.question: How should {name} support the presenter?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Listen with attentive, encouraging eye contact, allowing them the time needed to articulate their ideas
rubric.note: Creates a supportive, patient audience environment.
rubric.keys: listen attentively|encouraging eye contact|patient listening

rubric.point: Supportively suggest a technical word if they look to the room for help, without taking over the presentation
rubric.keys: suggest word gently|collaborative support|do not take over

rubric.point: Applaud enthusiastically for the quality of the solar irrigation concept once the presentation concludes
rubric.note: Celebrates substantive scientific ideas over linguistic polish.
rubric.keys: applaud concept quality|celebrate ideas

dangerous: giggle at grammatical stumbles
tell teacher to disqualify the speaker
mimic their pronunciation

sources.name: NCERT - Inclusive Education in Indian Classrooms

cards.title: Accessibility for all: Keeping ramps, corridors, and doors open
facts: Universal design and accessibility are human rights: ramps, wide doors, elevators, and tactile paving allow all citizens full participation.
Parking bicycles in front of ramps, cluttering corridors, or misusing accessible restrooms creates insurmountable barriers for disabled peers.
do: Never park bicycles, scooters, or sports gear across wheelchair ramps or curb cuts
Hold heavy doors open when you see someone using crutches, a wheelchair, or carrying heavy boxes
Keep accessible restroom stalls available for individuals who genuinely require their grab rails and turning radius
dont: Never use accessible wheelchair ramps as skate ramps or obstacle courses
Never crowd elevator doors when a student with mobility aids is trying to enter

myths.statement: Accessible ramps are just decorative architectural features that school skate clubs can use for stunts.
myths.truth: Ramps and tactile paving are vital lifelines that ensure citizens with disabilities can access education, transit, and healthcare.

quiz.q: Why is it critical to keep yellow tactile paving stones on sidewalks and railway stations completely clear of obstacles?
options: Because they look nice when clean
Because visually impaired citizens rely on tactile bumps to navigate safely with white canes
Because they are made of gold
Because trains park on them
quiz.explanation: Tactile paving guides visually impaired pedestrians away from hazards; blocking them causes painful collisions.

situations: Outside the school auditorium at {at}, students leave ten bicycles leaning directly against the wheelchair access ramp.
scenario.question: How should {name} demonstrate civic accessibility awareness?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Help move the bicycles safely away from the ramp into the designated cycle parking zone
rubric.note: Removes physical barrier to ensure universal access.
rubric.keys: move bicycles away|clear access ramp|designated parking

rubric.point: Remind classmates politely that blocking ramps prevents peers in wheelchairs from entering the auditorium
rubric.note: Educates peers on disability rights and physical access.
rubric.keys: educate classmates|blocking ramps prevents access

rubric.point: Suggest to school administration that clear 'Keep Ramp Clear' signage be painted on the ground
rubric.keys: suggest keep ramp clear signs|infrastructural fix

dangerous: leave bikes blocking ramp
add your own bike to the pile
mock disabled peers for complaining

cards.title: Invisible disabilities: ADHD, Autism, and Dyslexia explained
facts: Many disabilities are invisible: ADHD, autism, dyslexia, epilepsy, chronic pain, and diabetes do not involve wheelchairs or white canes.
Neurodiversity recognizes that human brains are wired differently; what looks like 'laziness' or 'acting weird' is often a neurological difference.
do: Never assume someone is faking difficulty just because 'they look completely normal'
Be patient if a neurodivergent peer needs instructions written down or avoids noisy, chaotic environments
Celebrate diverse cognitive strengths: dyslexic thinkers often excel in spatial reasoning, while autistic peers excel in deep focus
dont: Never mock a classmate who flaps their hands, rocks, or wears noise-canceling headphones to self-soothe
Never use diagnostic terms like 'Autistic' or 'ADHD' as casual playground insults

myths.statement: If someone can walk and talk normally, it is impossible for them to have a genuine disability.
myths.truth: Over 80% of disabilities are invisible, including learning differences, autoimmune conditions, and sensory processing disorders.

options: A disease that needs to be cured with pills
The understanding that brain differences (like autism and ADHD) are natural variations of the human genome, not personal defects
A computer programming language
A school for doctors
quiz.explanation: Neurodiversity views brain differences through the lens of human diversity and strength rather than deficit.

situations: In class at {at}, an autistic student rocks gently in their chair and wears ear-defenders during loud group activities, prompting whispers from peers.
scenario.question: How should {name} foster an inclusive environment?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Treat the classmate with warm, respectful normality and normalize sensory regulation tools
rubric.keys: treat with respect|normalize ear defenders|sensory regulation

rubric.point: Gently explain to curious peers that loud noise can cause sensory overload and ear defenders help them focus
rubric.keys: explain sensory overload|educate peers|dispel whispers

rubric.point: Include the classmate in project discussions by communicating clearly without chaotic shouting
rubric.note: Adapts group work for inclusive participation.
rubric.keys: clear communication|inclusive group work

dangerous: mock the classmate's rocking
pull off their ear defenders
demand they act normal

sources.name: National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities

cards.title: Names and dignity: The deep sting of derogatory nicknames
facts: Calling someone by a cruel nickname based on their weight, skin shade, caste, region, or disability is verbal violence that erodes self-esteem.
Even if the person smiles or laughs along awkwardly, inside they often feel humiliated, diminished, and deeply unsafe.
do: Always address peers by their real, preferred name or an affectionate nickname they genuinely love
If someone says 'Please don't call me that', stop immediately and permanently—no debate, no excuses
Notice nervous laughter: victims often smile to avoid escalating conflict, not because they find the nickname funny
dont: Never use nicknames that reference someone's body size, glasses, dental braces, or skin tone
Never justify cruelty with 'It's just an affectionate nickname bro'

myths.statement: If a classmate smiles when you call them a cruel nickname about their weight, it proves they genuinely enjoy it.
myths.truth: Smiling is a common appeasement response to survive social humiliation. Forcing cruel labels damages human dignity.

quiz.q: What should you do if you realize a nickname you frequently use makes a classmate feel uncomfortable or sad?
options: Tell them they are too sensitive and keep using it
Apologize sincerely, stop using the nickname immediately, and address them by their chosen name
Use it even louder in front of teachers
Make up a worse nickname
quiz.explanation: True maturity means respecting other people's dignity and dropping hurtful labels instantly.

situations: In the playground at {at}, several boys repeatedly call a classmate 'Chashmish' and 'Mota', while the classmate looks down with a forced, uncomfortable smile.
scenario.question: How should {name} intervene constructively?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Ask the classmate privately what they actually prefer to be called and start using their real name consistently
rubric.note: Validates their true personal identity and dignity.
rubric.keys: ask preferred name|use real name consistently|restore dignity

rubric.point: Tell the group firmly: 'Hey guys, call him by his actual name, let's drop the nicknames'
rubric.note: Sets a clear, respectful peer standard.
rubric.keys: call him by real name|drop nicknames|firm boundary

rubric.point: Never join in repeating the derogatory label
rubric.keys: refuse to repeat nickname|lead by example

dangerous: call him worse names
tell him to get thicker skin
laugh along with the bullies

sources.name: CBSE Guidelines on Prevention of Bullying in Schools

cards.title: Lunchbox diplomacy: Respecting diverse dietary traditions and foods
facts: Food is an intimate expression of culture, family heritage, regional agriculture, and religious traditions.
Making disgusted faces or saying 'Eww, what stinks?' at someone's traditional home-cooked lunch causes deep cultural shame and alienation.
do: Approach unfamiliar lunch dishes with curiosity rather than disgust: 'That smells aromatic, what dish is that?'
Respect diverse dietary boundaries (vegetarian, Jain, halal, egg-free, allergies) without mocking or tampering with food
Practice hygienic sharing: offer food politely without touching someone else's lunchbox with unwashed fingers
dont: Never say 'Eww gross!' to someone eating their family's traditional home-cooked meal
Never trick a vegetarian or religious peer into eating meat, eggs, or ingredients they abstain from

myths.statement: Tricking a strict vegetarian friend into eating chicken nuggets by lying about the ingredients is a hilarious, harmless prank.
myths.truth: Deceiving someone about what they eat violates their bodily autonomy, religious beliefs, and can trigger severe allergic reactions.

quiz.q: What is the most respectful attitude toward a classmate's unfamiliar regional lunchbox dish?
options: Screaming that it smells disgusting and running away
Asking with genuine polite curiosity about what ingredients and spices were used in the dish
Throwing it in the trash
Forcing them to eat your food instead
quiz.explanation: Culinary curiosity celebrates cultural diversity and turns meal breaks into opportunities for shared friendship.

situations: At the lunch table at {at}, a student opens a tiffin box with fermented regional bamboo shoots and fish, and classmates make gagging noises.
scenario.question: How should {name} model inclusive lunchbox diplomacy?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Shut down the mockery and ask the classmate with curiosity: 'What is this regional specialty called?'
rubric.note: Models cultural openness and halts humiliation.
rubric.keys: shut down mockery|ask with curiosity|cultural openness

rubric.point: Explain to peers that every culture has unique fermented, pickled, or spiced foods that taste delicious
rubric.keys: explain diverse food traditions|educate peers

rubric.point: Ensure the lunch table remains a warm, welcoming space where all food traditions are honored
rubric.keys: warm welcoming lunch table|honor all traditions

dangerous: yell that the food is stinky
demand they move to another table
spit on the tiffin box

sources.name: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat - Cultural Understanding Initiatives

cards.title: Celebrating India's mosaic: Embracing diverse festivals with joy
facts: India's cultural genius lies in its pluralism: Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Gurpurab, Onam, Pongal, Bihu, and Chhath Puja reflect shared humanity.
Participating in or wishing peers joy during their festivals strengthens community fabric and builds broad-minded global citizens.
do: Wish your classmates joy on their cultural and religious festivals (e.g., 'Eid Mubarak', 'Happy Gurpurab', 'Merry Christmas')
Learn the meaning and history behind regional festivals: harvest gratitude, victory of truth over darkness, or universal charity
Share festive sweets (mithai, sewaiyan, plum cake, payasam) with warmth and mutual affection
dont: Never insult or belittle another community's sacred rituals, prayer customs, or traditional attire
Never divide school friendship circles along religious, caste, or regional fault lines

myths.statement: You are only allowed to learn about or celebrate the specific festivals practiced by your own immediate family.
myths.truth: India's greatest strength is composite culture. Sharing the joy of our neighbors' festivals enriches our own understanding of humanity.

quiz.q: What shared universal theme unites diverse Indian harvest and light festivals across all regions?
options: Competition over who buys the most plastic
Gratitude to nature, the triumph of light and justice, and sharing prosperity with community
Staying angry at neighbors
Refusing to share sweets
quiz.explanation: Across every state and faith, Indian festivals celebrate ecological gratitude, light over darkness, and shared community generosity.

situations: In the school courtyard at {at}, students from diverse backgrounds are talking about upcoming festive holidays (Diwali, Eid, and Christmas).
scenario.question: How can {name} celebrate this cultural mosaic?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Ask friends about their favorite family customs, recipes, and childhood memories during their holidays
rubric.note: Deepens mutual respect through genuine personal storytelling.
rubric.keys: ask about family customs|recipes|shared storytelling

rubric.point: Wish classmates warm greetings on their festive days and share traditional festive treats happily
rubric.keys: warm greetings|share festive treats|celebrate together

rubric.point: Appreciate how India's multi-faith heritage makes our classrooms vibrant, colorful, and resilient
rubric.keys: appreciate multi-faith heritage|national harmony

dangerous: mock religious traditions you dont practice
refuse to eat sweets from other communities
argue over which festival is superior

sources.name: Ministry of Culture - Composite Culture of India

cards.title: The gift of presence: Listening with your whole heart
facts: Most people do not listen to understand; they listen only to reply, interrupt, or offer unsolicited advice.
Active empathetic listening means giving your complete attention, withholding judgment, and letting the other person feel truly heard.
do: Put away your smartphone, lean slightly forward, and maintain warm eye contact when someone is confiding in you
Summarize what you hear: 'It sounds like you felt really betrayed when that happened, is that right?'
Avoid jumping in with immediate advice unless they explicitly ask: 'What do you think I should do?'
dont: Never interrupt someone in the middle of their sentence to talk about your own life experiences
Never dismiss someone's feelings with 'Oh that's nothing, listen to what happened to me!'

myths.statement: Being a great listener means immediately interrupting with a 10-step plan to solve all their problems.
myths.truth: People in emotional distress need connection and understanding first, not a lecture. Listening without fixing is the deepest gift.

quiz.q: Which conversational response shows authentic empathetic listening?
options: 'That's completely your fault'
'That sounds really overwhelming; I'm so glad you shared that with me, I'm here for you'
'Whatever, can I tell you my story now?'
'You should just stop being sad'
quiz.explanation: Validating feelings and offering presence without judgment creates emotional safety and deep trust.

scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

cards.title: Releasing grudges: The liberating strength of forgiveness
facts: Holding onto a bitter grudge is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to suffer.
Forgiveness does not mean accepting ongoing abuse or pretending bad behavior is okay; it means releasing toxic hatred so you can heal.
do: Distinguish forgiveness from weakness: letting go of rage requires immense inner strength and emotional maturity
Focus on resolving conflicts using 'I-messages': 'I felt hurt when you broke your promise, can we talk about it?'
Set healthy boundaries: you can forgive someone while deciding not to be their close partner until trust is rebuilt
dont: Never nurse silent revenge fantasies that keep you locked in bitterness and stress
Never use social exile or group ostracization as a weapon against a classmate who made a mistake

myths.statement: Forgiving a classmate who hurt you means you must let them treat you like a doormat forever.
myths.truth: Forgiveness frees your heart from toxic bitterness; boundaries determine how close that person is allowed to get in the future.

quiz.q: What is the healthiest reason to forgive someone who apologized for hurting you?
options: Because you want them to owe you money
To liberate your own mind from toxic bitterness, reduce stress, and restore personal peace
Because teachers forced you to shake hands
So you can plot revenge later
quiz.explanation: Forgiveness is an act of self-care that frees your emotional energy from the grip of past hurt.

situations: Following a bitter disagreement over a science fair presentation at {at}, a teammate apologizes sincerely for snapping in anger.
scenario.question: How should {name} navigate this conflict resolution?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Accept the apology gracefully, acknowledging that everyone makes mistakes under pressure
rubric.keys: accept apology gracefully|acknowledge stress|forgive mistake

rubric.point: Share calmly how the outburst felt so mutual understanding is established before moving forward
rubric.keys: communicate impact calmly|clear the air

rubric.point: Rebuild the collaborative relationship with clear, fair ground rules for future team meetings
rubric.keys: clear ground rules|rebuild partnership

dangerous: hold a grudge for the rest of the year
tell everyone in school never to talk to that peer
demand revenge

cards.title: Inclusive teamwork: Thriving together in mixed-ability groups
facts: Classrooms bring together diverse strengths: some peers excel in writing, others in visual sketching, math, or oral presentation.
Inclusive teams do not dump all the work on the highest-scoring student; they structure tasks so every member contributes with pride.
do: Map team roles to individual talents: visual charts, speech delivery, factual research, and physical building
Support peers who struggle with specific academic tasks by breaking steps into manageable chunks
Celebrate the collective victory of the entire team rather than claiming individual dominance
dont: Never sideline or exclude a team member who has learning differences or lower exam marks
Never do all the project work in secret and hand in the project without involving your teammates

myths.statement: The fastest and best way to complete a group project is for the top student to do 100% of the work while everyone else watches.
myths.truth: Group projects teach real-world collaborative leadership, delegation, and mutual empowerment—not solo heroism.

quiz.q: What is the primary responsibility of a student team captain in a mixed-ability group project?
options: To scream at everyone until they obey
To identify each teammate's unique strength and empower everyone to make a meaningful contribution
To do the entire project alone overnight
To take all the stage credit
quiz.explanation: True leadership unlocks the potential of every team member, ensuring everyone learns and contributes.

scenario.question: How should {name} structure the project for inclusive success?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Collaborate on speech practice patiently, creating supportive cue cards with bullet points
rubric.keys: speech practice|accessible cue cards|patient support

rubric.point: Ensure every team member presents a meaningful section of the display during teacher evaluation
rubric.note: Guarantees shared dignity and stage presence.
rubric.keys: shared presentation|meaningful section for all

complain to teacher that team is weak

cards.title: Seva and volunteering: Humility in community action
facts: Volunteering at animal shelters, elder care homes, or community soup kitchens connects us to the larger human family.
True service (Seva) is performed with humility and respect, never as a self-aggrandizing photo-op for social media likes.
do: Approach community service with a posture of learning and listening rather than acting like a wealthy savior
Focus on the real needs of the community: cleaning, serving food, reading books to elders, or sorting relief materials
Keep mobile phones in your pocket; never take exploitative selfies with vulnerable children or elders
dont: Never treat volunteering purely as an empty resume-polishing exercise without genuine compassion
Never look down on the communities you are serving with pity or condescension

myths.statement: Taking photos of yourself handing bananas to impoverished children and posting them on Instagram is the definition of true charity.
myths.truth: Exploitative 'poverty tourism' robs vulnerable people of their human dignity. Authentic service is done with quiet humility and respect.

quiz.q: What is the traditional Indian concept of 'Seva' (selfless service)?
options: Hiring people to clean your room
Serving the community selflessly with humility, without expecting personal fame, wealth, or social media applause
Running for political office
Giving away expired canned food
quiz.explanation: Authentic Seva dissolves human ego and builds deep solidarity with all living beings.

rubric.point: Serve food with warm smiles, eye contact, and genuine humility

cards.title: The power of the upstander: Standing united against prejudice
facts: Prejudice and discrimination thrive when good people stand by silently and do nothing.
An 'Upstander' is someone who recognizes injustice, speaks up safely, supports the victim, and refuses to let hatred become normal.
do: Use the 4 Ds of intervention: Direct (speak up), Distract (interrupt with a question), Delegate (get help), Delay (support victim after)
Stand physically beside the targeted peer so they know they are not alone against the crowd
Report hate speech, casteist slurs, and religious discrimination to school leaders and parents immediately
dont: Never be a silent bystander whose silence gives permission to bigots and bullies
Never put your own physical life in extreme danger; use distraction or get adult intervention when violence threatens

myths.statement: If you see a classmate being targeted with hate slurs, staying silent is the best way to remain neutral and fair.
myths.truth: Silence always helps the oppressor, never the victim. Staying neutral in situations of injustice means siding with the bully.

quiz.q: Which of the following describes an effective 'Distraction' tactic to interrupt bullying without physical confrontation?
options: Joining in the insults
Walking up to the targeted peer and asking: 'Hey, our science teacher is looking for you in Lab 2, can you come now?'
Throwing rocks at the bullies
Laughing loudly
quiz.explanation: Distraction interrupts the harassment dynamic cleanly, giving the victim a safe exit without escalating violence.

situations: In the school bus at {at}, older students corner a younger student from a minority community, hurling discriminatory slurs and threats.
scenario.question: How should {name} act as an upstander?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Use the Delegate strategy: alert the bus conductor and driver immediately that bullying is happening
rubric.note: Delegates intervention to authority figures for immediate safety.
rubric.keys: alert bus driver and conductor|delegate intervention|immediate safety

rubric.point: Walk over, sit beside the younger student, and say: 'Hey, sit with me up front, you are safe here'
rubric.note: Provides immediate physical solidarity and protective presence.
rubric.keys: sit beside student|you are safe here|protective solidarity

rubric.point: Report the specific discriminatory incident to school administration the following morning
rubric.note: Holds perpetrators accountable through official channels.
rubric.keys: report to school administration|hold accountable

dangerous: join in chanting hate slurs
look down at phone pretending not to notice
encourage the bullies
